editorial_note: GitHub listed sixteen projects this Friday morning, and seven of them were featured here in the past week. Today's six picks start with ==nginx 1.31.9, which fixes ten security vulnerabilities==, then Firecrawl's new local scraping binary, the OpenSRE agent for failed CI runs, an App Store and Google Play rejection guard, an agent skill that draws editorial diagrams, and AutoClip, a desktop tool that cuts long videos into short clips. Curation order reflects practical interest, not GitHub rank. Trending is not a release date or an endorsement.

projects.description: The official NGINX open-source web server and reverse proxy: mainline release 1.31.9, published on 18 November, ==fixes ten security vulnerabilities== across HTTP/2, HTTP/3, the resolver, the mail proxy and the stream modules.
projects.why_interesting: nginx.org's advisories page rates three of the ten as major: ==memory corruption in HTTP/2 flow control==, an infinite loop while reading a request body over TLS 1.3, and a use-after-free in the mail proxy. Most affect versions going back years, and the same page lists the stable line as fixed from 1.30.7, so this is a patch-now item for anyone running nginx at the edge.
projects.caveat: The advisories page lists the affected version ranges and fixed releases, but ==no exploit details were checked here==. Distribution packages and vendor builds may ship the fixes under different version numbers, so check your own package source rather than the upstream version string.

projects.description: A web scraping and crawling service for AI agents: it turns websites into clean Markdown, and its new ==Firecrawl Local is a single binary== that scrapes, crawls and maps sites from your own machine.
projects.why_interesting: Firecrawl Local landed in the repository on 11 November and reached 0.1.1 on 18 November. The README says it needs ==no database, queue or container==, renders JavaScript pages in the Chrome already on the machine, parses PDFs and Office files locally, and can serve the Firecrawl v2 API on localhost, so code written for the hosted service can run against it.
projects.caveat: The project is mainly ==AGPL-3.0==, which matters if you modify it and offer it as a network service; the SDKs are MIT. Search and the 550+ data providers go to Firecrawl Cloud, its init command edits the MCP configs of several AI tools, and the README leaves respecting each site's terms to the user.

projects.description: A command-line agent for broken CI builds: OpenSRE ==reads the failed run, traces the cause and pushes a fix== for you to review, self-hosted and with your own models.
projects.why_interesting: Most CI tooling stops at a red mark. OpenSRE aims at the next step, separating CI-caused failures from code-caused ones, and the README promises reporting on failure rates and hours lost to unreliable CI. It ships dated builds almost daily; the latest, 0.1.2026.11.20, appeared this morning.
projects.caveat: The README calls it a ==public alpha== whose APIs and integrations may change. The suggested install pipes a remote script to the shell and fetches the latest build from main, the agent pushes code to your repository, and product analytics and Sentry error reports are opt-out rather than opt-in.

projects.description: A pre-submission guard for mobile apps: a playbook and shell script that scan an iOS or Android project for ==common App Store and Google Play rejection causes== before you submit.
projects.why_interesting: Rejections cost days of review time, and the README maps each pattern to a guideline and a fix, covering demo accounts, privacy manifests and Data safety declarations first. It can also install as a hook in many AI coding tools, so an agent's submit command is blocked while a critical risk stands.
projects.caveat: The licence is the ==OpenRoots Agent License 2.3, not an OSI open-source licence==: free below USD 20 million in annual revenue, a royalty above it, and no right to use it for AI training. The installer edits hook settings in many agent configs, and the README's statistics are the author's claims.

projects.description: An agent skill that draws diagrams: it writes ==one self-contained HTML and SVG file== per diagram, in your own brand colours and fonts, for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and other hosts.
projects.why_interesting: Instead of Mermaid output, the agent picks among 51 diagram types, from architecture and sequence to quadrants and schedules, states its plan and writes a file you open by double-clicking. It can import draw.io, Mermaid, Excalidraw and PlantUML sources, and its privacy policy says it has ==no server, accounts or telemetry==.
projects.caveat: Diagrams load fonts from Google Fonts unless you ask for system fonts, and brand onboarding has your agent fetch pages from the site you name. The repository description says 45 types while the README says 51, and the quality of each diagram still depends on the agent and model running it.

projects.description: A desktop tool that turns long videos into short clips: paste a link or file, pick a platform, and AutoClip ==cuts up to ten clips with subtitles, covers and post text== for Douyin, Xiaohongshu, TikTok, Reels, Shorts, Bilibili or YouTube.
projects.why_interesting: Cutting, speaker framing and rendering run on your own computer, and the analysis model is your choice, including local models through Ollama or LM Studio. The README's cost table gives text-model costs of under one yuan per long video, measured by the maintainer on one Apple Silicon Mac; a CLI and an MCP server share the same pipeline.
projects.caveat: The desktop app is for ==macOS on Apple Silicon or Windows x64== only. Cloud analysis sends captions, sample frames or audio to the provider you configure and is billed by usage, and you need the rights to the videos you cut; the cost and time figures are the maintainer's own measurements.
